DDM-BM-01: diff two 5-field JSON objects (1 field differs).

detaileddescription.para: Measures the hot-path diff latency for a minimal document payload. Useful as a low-baseline reference for overhead decomposition.

briefdescription.para: DDM-BM-02: diff two 100-field JSON objects (50 fields differ).

detaileddescription.para: Exercises the full field-scan loop across a realistic large payload. Result feeds GATE-DOC-01 (p99 ≤ 500 µs).

briefdescription.para: DDM-BM-03: three-way merge — ours and theirs modify different fields.

detaileddescription.para: No conflict is generated; FAIL strategy confirms clean-merge semantics on every iteration. Result feeds GATE-DOC-02 (p99 ≤ 200 µs).

briefdescription.para: DDM-BM-04: three-way merge — 50 conflicting fields, OURS_WINS strategy.

detaileddescription.para: All 50 fields conflict; every conflict is resolved automatically with OURS_WINS. Measures combined conflict-detection and resolution cost.

briefdescription.para: DDM-BM-05: three-way merge — 50 conflicting fields, THEIRS_WINS.

detaileddescription.para: Symmetric variant of DDM-BM-04. Confirms THEIRS_WINS resolution cost matches OURS_WINS; both paths should be within 5% of each other.

briefdescription.para: DDM-BM-06: three-way merge — 50 conflicting fields, FAIL strategy.

detaileddescription.para: Exercises the error path: every iteration returns ERR_DOC_MERGE_CONFLICT. Measures conflict detection + error construction cost without resolution. The error result is DoNotOptimize'd to prevent elision.

briefdescription.para: DDM-BM-07: diff two empty JSON objects.

detaileddescription.para: Measures the fixed overhead of the diff path when both documents are empty. Used as a lower-bound baseline for overhead decomposition.

briefdescription.para: DDM-BM-08: merge where base = ours = theirs (zero divergence).

detaileddescription.para: Exercises the no-change fast path in computeMerge. All three versions are identical so no conflict or change is detected.

briefdescription.para: Release gate verification for GATE-DOC-01.

detaileddescription.para: Runs the 100-field diff workload (DDM-BM-02 payload) and asserts that the mean per-iteration latency is within the 500 µs hard gate. The gate value is published as a benchmark counter for automated release manifest comparison.

simplesect.para: Mean latency in a controlled CPU-pinned environment serves as a conservative proxy for p99. For formal p99 attestation run with benchmark_repetitions=10 and post-process with report_variance.py.

briefdescription.para: Release gate verification for GATE-DOC-02.

detaileddescription.para: Runs the clean-merge workload (DDM-BM-03 payload: 10 fields/branch, no conflict) and asserts that mean latency is within the 200 µs hard gate.

briefdescription.para: RTP-BM-01: beginRelay() throughput for sequential relay IDs.

detaileddescription.para: Each iteration creates a new relay with a unique ID derived from an atomic counter. Measures the combined cost of snapshot ID construction, JSON body assembly, and InMemoryDocumentStore::put().
Result feeds GATE-DOC-03 (p99 ≤ 1 ms).

briefdescription.para: RTP-BM-02: saveInteraction() throughput — 10 sequential interactions.

detaileddescription.para: Each iteration: (paused) begin a fresh relay, then (measured) save 10 interactions sequentially. PauseTiming() guards the beginRelay() setup call so only the saveInteraction() loop is measured.
Reports items_processed as iterations × 10 for ops/s computation.

briefdescription.para: RTP-BM-03: loadInteraction() latency for a pre-populated relay.

detaileddescription.para: Loads interaction index 5 (mid-range) from the pre-populated relay on every iteration. The relay contains 11 snapshots; load is a pure read path through InMemoryDocumentStore::get().
Result feeds GATE-DOC-04 (p99 ≤ 200 µs).

briefdescription.para: RTP-BM-04: countSnapshots() latency for a relay with 10 snapshots.

detaileddescription.para: Calls countSnapshots() on the pre-populated relay (11 total snapshots). Internally lists the collection and scans all IDs for the relay prefix.

briefdescription.para: RTP-BM-05: end-to-end relay workflow — begin + 5x save + 5x load.

detaileddescription.para: Each iteration: (paused) allocate a unique relay ID, then (measured) call beginRelay(), save 5 interactions, and load all 5 back. Represents the complete hot path of the DELEGATE-52 round-trip use case.
Reports items_processed as iterations × 11 (1 begin + 5 save + 5 load).

briefdescription.para: RTP-BM-06: makeSnapshotId-equivalent string construction throughput.

detaileddescription.para: Benchmarks the zero-padded snapshot ID construction pattern used internally by StoreBackedRoundTripEditor::makeSnapshotId(). Since makeSnapshotId() is private, the equivalent ostringstream construction is measured directly.
At 1M iterations this benchmark reveals allocator and ostringstream overhead in the snapshot ID hot path.

briefdescription.para: RTP-BM-07: saveInteraction() with a 10 KB document string.

detaileddescription.para: Each iteration: (paused) begin a relay, then (measured) save one 10 KB document snapshot. Measures JSON body assembly and in-memory store insertion cost under a realistic large-document payload.

briefdescription.para: RTP-BM-08: two concurrent relay workloads via std::thread.

detaileddescription.para: Each benchmark iteration launches two threads; each thread independently begins a relay, saves 5 interactions, and loads one snapshot. The threads share the InMemoryDocumentStore (which is protected by its internal mutex) and the StoreBackedRoundTripEditor.
Measures the overhead of concurrent write+read access under the store's mutex. Reports items_processed as iterations × 2 (two workloads/iter).

briefdescription.para: Release gate verification for GATE-DOC-03.

detaileddescription.para: Runs the beginRelay() workload and asserts that mean latency is within the 1 ms (1000 µs) hard gate. The gate value is published as a benchmark counter for automated release manifest comparison.

briefdescription.para: Release gate verification for GATE-DOC-04.

detaileddescription.para: Runs the loadInteraction() workload on the pre-populated relay and asserts that mean latency is within the 200 µs hard gate.

briefdescription.para: DST-BM-01: put() throughput — kBatchSize sequential documents per iteration.

detaileddescription.para: Each iteration inserts kBatchSize documents with unique IDs derived from iterCounter_ to guarantee no ERR_DOC_ALREADY_EXISTS errors. Measures raw JSON-body storage throughput.
Result feeds GATE-DOC-05 (throughput ≥ 100 000 ops/s).

briefdescription.para: DST-BM-02: get() latency — random access into 1000-document store.

detaileddescription.para: Each iteration performs one get() using a deterministic pseudo-random key drawn from the pre-loaded collection. Measures point-lookup latency under a realistic working-set size.
Result feeds GATE-DOC-06 (p99 ≤ 100 µs).

briefdescription.para: DST-BM-03: list() throughput — enumerate 1000 document IDs.

detaileddescription.para: Calls list() on a 1000-document collection on every iteration. Exercises the full collection-scan hot path in InMemoryDocumentStore.

briefdescription.para: DST-BM-04: count() latency — count 1000-document collection.

detaileddescription.para: Calls count() on the 1000-document pre-loaded collection. Internally this scans the store map to count keys matching the collection prefix.

briefdescription.para: DST-BM-05: update() body replacement throughput — 1000 existing docs.

detaileddescription.para: Each iteration updates all kPreloadCount documents in kReadCollection with a fresh JSON body. Measures the combined JSON replacement and unordered_map lookup cost across 1000 records.
Reports items_processed as iterations × kPreloadCount.

briefdescription.para: DST-BM-06: remove() throughput — kBatchSize documents per iteration.

detaileddescription.para: Each iteration: (paused) inserts kBatchSize documents with unique IDs, then (measured) removes all of them. PauseTiming guards the pre-insertion so only the remove() path is timed.
Reports items_processed as iterations × kBatchSize.

briefdescription.para: DST-BM-07: put() with a 10 KB JSON body document.

detaileddescription.para: Each iteration inserts one document with a 10 KB body (pre-built in SetUp) using a unique ID derived from iterCounter_. Measures JSON copy and unordered_map insertion overhead under a large-body payload.

briefdescription.para: DST-BM-08: validate() throughput — 1000 documents against 10-field schema.

detaileddescription.para: Each iteration validates kPreloadCount pre-built document bodies against the sealed 10-field schema registered at version 1. Measures the combined cost of schema lookup and per-field type/presence checking.
Reports items_processed as iterations × kPreloadCount.

briefdescription.para: Release gate verification for GATE-DOC-05.

detaileddescription.para: Runs the single-document put() workload and asserts that the measured throughput meets the 100 000 ops/s minimum. The gate is evaluated from items_processed / elapsed_time.

briefdescription.para: Release gate verification for GATE-DOC-06.

detaileddescription.para: Runs the random-access get() workload against the 1000-document pre-loaded collection and asserts that mean latency is within the 100 µs hard gate.
